key_headlines.title: South Korea's Q2 GDP Growth Surpasses Expectations at 0.6%
key_headlines.summary: Korea's economy grew 0.6% quarter-over-quarter in Q2 2026, significantly exceeding the Bank of Korea's forecast of 0.2%, driven by strong semiconductor exports that offset Middle East geopolitical risks. This marks the second consecutive quarter of robust growth following Q1's 1.8% expansion.

key_headlines.title: Government Launches Sixth Real Estate Policy with Comprehensive Tax Measures
key_headlines.summary: President Lee Jae-myung unveiled the sixth major real estate policy since taking office, integrating taxation, housing supply, and financial measures through a national policy forum. The comprehensive approach aims to stabilize housing prices amid supply constraints and rising prices in the Seoul metropolitan area.

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Boom May Enable Korea to Achieve 4% Per Capita GNI and 3% Annual Growth
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's semiconductor exports surged 199.5% in Q2, driving economic growth and real income gains at their highest levels since 1988. The government now sees increased possibility of achieving 3% annual growth, though disparities remain with construction and agriculture sectors declining.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Index Recovers 7,000 Mark After 5 Trading Days with 4.4% Surge
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index surged 4.4% to close at 7,096.89, reclaiming the 7,000 level after five trading days, while KOSDAQ rose 5% as AI-related investor sentiment recovered. The market rally reflected optimism following positive economic data and ahead of the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting.

key_headlines.title: Fixed-Rate Mortgages Now 1% Higher Than Variable Rates, Increasing Borrower Dilemma
key_headlines.summary: With the Bank of Korea raising its base rate for the first time in three and a half years, borrowers face difficult decisions between fixed and variable-rate mortgages. The 1% spread between fixed and variable rates at major banks creates tension between immediate interest savings and long-term rate risk.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy delivered a surprise performance in Q2 2026 with 0.6% growth, significantly exceeding the Bank of Korea's 0.2% forecast and marking the second consecutive quarter of expansion. Strong semiconductor exports, which grew 199.5%, proved instrumental in offsetting geopolitical headwinds from Middle East tensions and rising oil prices. The growth momentum has strengthened prospects for achieving 3% annual growth, with real income gains reaching their highest levels since 1988. However, the gains remain concentrated in semiconductors, with construction, agriculture, and fisheries sectors experiencing contraction, illustrating a K-shaped recovery pattern.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea's announcement of Q2 GDP growth at 0.6% has significantly improved prospects for annual growth targets, with government officials now confident about achieving 3% expansion. The strong performance reflects robust exports and domestic demand working in tandem, supported by supplementary budget measures. Real GNI (Gross National Income) growth reached its highest level in 38 years, driven largely by semiconductor price increases. However, the uneven sectoral performance highlights structural imbalances in the economy, as semiconductor-dependent growth masks weakness in traditional industries. The central bank's recent base rate increase signals confidence in the recovery but adds uncertainty to future growth prospects.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korea's stock market demonstrated strong momentum on July 23, with the KOSPI surging 4.4% to close at 7,096.89, reclaiming the 7,000 level after five trading days, while the KOSDAQ index rose 5%. Recovery in AI-related investor sentiment drove the rally, with major banks like KB Financial and Shinhan Financial posting record profits from rising interest rates and increased brokerage activity. Ahead of the Federal Reserve's July 28-29 FOMC meeting, South Korean investors closely monitored potential U.S. rate hikes, with concerns also reflected in cryptocurrency markets as Bitcoin declined to the 65,000 dollar level. Foreign investors were noted selling U.S. Treasury bonds preemptively ahead of anticipated rate increases.
sections.Industry & Technology: LG Energy Solution expanded its patent infringement litigation against Chinese battery manufacturer EVE Energy to the United States, with filings at the International Trade Commission and Texas federal court, broadening disputes beyond pouch and prismatic batteries to cylindrical formats. LG Energy Solution partnered with Chungbuk National University, Chungcheongbuk Province, and industry associations to develop specialized battery industry talent through government-supported regional human resource training programs. LS Electric reported record Q2 operating profit of 178.5 billion won, benefiting from surging AI data center investment demand that bolstered power infrastructure and advanced equipment divisions. The battery and power infrastructure sectors are experiencing robust growth as AI data center expansion accelerates globally.
sections.Real Estate: President Lee Jae-myung held a national forum on real estate policy on July 23, unveiling the government's sixth comprehensive policy package combining taxation, supply expansion, and financial measures to stabilize housing prices. The president acknowledged limitations in reconstruction and redevelopment projects for housing supply, noting that such projects often fail to increase household counts meaningfully due to increased unit sizes and resident displacement. A financial research institute proposed a 1% macroprudential management surcharge on high-value mortgages alongside interest payments to moderate excessive debt growth. The surge in rental market migration, with monthly rentals now comprising 68.6% of all lease transactions, reflects severe jeonse (deposit lease) shortage and tightening loan regulations that limit buyer financing capacity.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Federal Reserve faces market scrutiny ahead of the July 28-29 FOMC meeting, with increasing probability of a rate hike weighing on global markets and commodities, including a rise in international crude oil prices that pressured the New York stock market. Federal Reserve Chairman Powell's recent communication strategy has created uncertainty, with the deletion of dovish language regarding rate cuts from the June FOMC statement signaling potential policy tightening despite earlier expectations of rate reductions. Bitcoin and other risk assets declined as markets priced in the probability of U.S. rate increases, with CME FedWatch Tool showing significant odds of tightening at the upcoming meeting. General Motors reported better-than-expected Q2 earnings, with the company benefiting from protective trade policies against Chinese connected vehicles and domestic EV support tailwinds.
sections.AI & Economy: Chuncheon's district heating energy fusion cluster emerged as a major investment destination for AI data centers, attracting significant interest from domestic and foreign companies seeking stable power supply and cooling infrastructure. SK Telecom established SK Hyper, a dedicated AI data center subsidiary, as Korea positions itself as a hub for Asian AI infrastructure alongside its semiconductor and physical AI megaprojects. Alphabet faced scrutiny over massive capital expenditure plans for AI infrastructure despite two decades of consistent cash surpluses, raising concerns about profitability amid rising interest rates and potential supply-demand imbalances in AI chips. LS Electric benefited from surging AI data center investment demand, posting record profits as global expansion of AI infrastructure accelerates, while government investment in physical AI automation for ports promises efficiency gains but risks displacing crane operators and cargo handlers.
sections.Others: OCI Holdings recovered profitability in Q2 2026, gaining the upper price limit following improved solar PV value chain expansion despite ongoing uncertainty from U.S. Trade Expansion Act Section 232 polysilicon investigation results due in August-September. Major investment firms KKR and Capital Group launched hybrid products combining public and private bonds targeting individual investors, reflecting growing demand for diversified credit exposure across sectors. SK Telecom and Lotte Department Store launched AI business ecosystems, with SK Hyper targeting Asia's AI infrastructure market and Lotte introducing an AI agent service streamlining vendor onboarding and consultation processes. The 2025 Economic Census marked completion of South Korea's comprehensive business survey covering 7.53 million establishments, incorporating AI and unmanned retail operations data to capture evolving economic structures.
